# Two-group random-intercept Gaussian study
# 4 observations per participant, marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4
# Constant mean group difference = 0.45
# Equal allocation, no missing data
# Analyze participant averages with two-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05
# Target: 90% power

# Parameters
m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1  # marginal SD
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
delta <- 0.45  # group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level
target_power <- 0.90

# Calculate variance components
# From ICC = sigma_i^2 / sigma_marginal^2
sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2  # between-participant variance
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2  # within-participant variance

cat("Variance components:\n")
cat("  Between-participant variance (σ²ᵢ):", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  Within-participant variance (σ²_within):", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Marginal variance (σ²_marginal):", sigma_marginal^2, "\n\n")

# SD of participant average
# Var(avg) = Var((y1+y2+y3+y4)/4)
#          = [σ²ᵢ + σ²_within] / 4  (averaging m observations under random intercept model)
# Under random intercept: Var(y_ij) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within = σ²_marginal
# More precisely: Var(avg_i) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within/m = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)

sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)

cat("SD of participant average:\n")
cat("  SD_avg = σ_marginal * √(ICC + (1-ICC)/m)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = 1 * √(0.4 + 0.6/4)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = √0.55 =", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Effective standardized difference (Cohen's d scale)
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effective standardized difference:\n")
cat("  d = Δ / SD_avg =", delta, "/", sd_avg, "=", effective_d, "\n\n")

# For a two-sample t-test with equal allocation (n per group, total N = 2n):
# Non-centrality parameter: λ = d * √(n/2) where n is per group
# df = 2n - 2

# Function to compute power for given n (per group)
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_level) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  # Non-central t critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_level / 2, df)
  # Power is P(|t| > t_crit | H1)
  power <- pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE) +
           pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n achieving target power
# Start with a reasonable range
n_candidates <- seq(10, 80, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_candidates, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target_power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- n_candidates[min_idx]
achieved_power <- powers[min_idx]

# Also check the preceding design
if (min_idx > 1) {
  preceding_n <- n_candidates[min_idx - 1]
  preceding_power <- powers[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  preceding_n <- NA
  preceding_power <- NA
}

cat("Power calculation results:\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Minimum integer n per group:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", achieved_power, "\n")
if (!is.na(preceding_n)) {
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", preceding_n, "):", preceding_power, "\n")
}
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n\n")

# Show a table around the minimum
n_table <- max(min_n - 3, 1):min(min_n + 3, 80)
power_table <- sapply(n_table, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

cat("Power curve around minimum:\n")
for (i in seq_along(n_table)) {
  marker <- if (n_table[i] == min_n) " ← SELECTED" else ""
  cat(sprintf("  n = %3d: power = %.6f%s\n", n_table[i], power_table[i], marker))
}

cat("\n")
cat("Study design summary:\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Sample size: ", min_n, "participants per group\n")
cat("Total participants: ", 2 * min_n, "\n")
cat("Total observations: ", 2 * min_n * m, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant: ", m, "\n")
cat("Marginal SD: ", sigma_marginal, "\n")
cat("ICC: ", rho, "\n")
cat("Group difference: ", delta, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average: ", sd_avg, "\n")
cat("Effective d: ", effective_d, "\n")
cat("Two-sided α: ", alpha, "\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", achieved_power, "\n")

# Independent verification using different computational pathway
# Study design:
# - Two groups (equal allocation)
# - 4 observations per participant
# - Marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4
# - Group difference = 0.45
# - Analyzed via pooled two-sample t-test on participant averages
# - Target: 90% power, α = 0.05 (two-sided)

library(stats)

# Step 1: Verify variance decomposition
m <- 4
sigma_marginal <- 1
rho <- 0.4  # ICC

# Under random-intercept model:
# Var(y_ij) = sigma_i^2 + sigma_within^2 = sigma_marginal^2
# ICC = sigma_i^2 / sigma_marginal^2

sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2

cat("Variance decomposition verification:\n")
cat("  σ²_i (between) =", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  σ²_within =", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Sum (marginal) =", sigma_i_sq + sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  ICC = σ²_i / σ²_marginal =", sigma_i_sq / sigma_marginal^2, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Variance of participant average
# When averaging m observations from random-intercept model:
# Var(ȳ_i) = Var((1/m) * Σ_j y_ij)
#          = (1/m^2) * Σ_j Cov(y_ij, y_ij) + (1/m^2) * Σ_{j≠k} Cov(y_ij, y_ik)
#          = (1/m^2) * m * (σ²_i + σ²_within) + (1/m^2) * m(m-1) * σ²_i
#          = (1/m) * (σ²_i + σ²_within) + ((m-1)/m) * σ²_i
#          = (1/m) * σ²_marginal + ((m-1)/m) * σ²_i
#          = σ²_marginal * (1/m + ((m-1)/m) * ICC)
#          = σ²_marginal * (1/m + (m-1)*ICC/m)
#          = σ²_marginal * (1 + (m-1)*ICC) / m

var_avg_formula1 <- sigma_marginal^2 * (1 + (m - 1) * rho) / m
sd_avg_formula1 <- sqrt(var_avg_formula1)

# Alternative formulation:
# Var(ȳ_i) = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)
var_avg_formula2 <- sigma_marginal^2 * (rho + (1 - rho) / m)
sd_avg_formula2 <- sqrt(var_avg_formula2)

cat("Variance of participant average (two equivalent formulas):\n")
cat("  Formula 1: σ²_avg = σ²_marginal * (1 + (m-1)*ICC) / m\n")
cat("    Var(ȳ_i) =", var_avg_formula1, "\n")
cat("    SD(ȳ_i) =", sd_avg_formula1, "\n")
cat("  Formula 2: σ²_avg = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)\n")
cat("    Var(ȳ_i) =", var_avg_formula2, "\n")
cat("    SD(ȳ_i) =", sd_avg_formula2, "\n")
cat("  Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(var_avg_formula1, var_avg_formula2)), "\n\n")

sd_avg <- sd_avg_formula1

# Step 3: Effective standardized difference (Cohen's d for t-test)
delta <- 0.45
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effective standardized difference:\n")
cat("  d = Δ / SD(ȳ_i) =", delta, "/", round(sd_avg, 10), "=", effective_d, "\n\n")

# Step 4: Power calculation for two-sample t-test
# For two groups with n per group, total N = 2n
# H0: μ_1 = μ_2, H1: μ_1 ≠ μ_2
# Under H1 with effect d and equal n:
# t ~ t(df = 2n-2, λ) where λ = d * sqrt(n/2)
# Power = P(|t| > t_crit | H1)

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90

compute_power_v2 <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_sig) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  
  # Two-tailed critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_sig / 2, df)
  
  # Power: probability that |t| exceeds critical value under H1
  # This is equivalent to P(t > t_crit | NCP=λ) + P(t < -t_crit | NCP=λ)
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
           pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  return(power)
}

# Test at candidate values around expected minimum
candidates <- 55:65
powers <- sapply(candidates, function(n) compute_power_v2(n, effective_d, alpha))

cat("Power curve (independent calculation):\n")

# Two-group random-intercept Gaussian study
# 4 observations per participant, marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4
# Constant mean group difference = 0.45
# Equal allocation, no missing data
# Analyze participant averages with two-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05
# Target: 90% power

# Parameters
m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1  # marginal SD
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
delta <- 0.45  # group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level
target_power <- 0.90

# Calculate variance components
# From ICC = sigma_i^2 / sigma_marginal^2
sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2  # between-participant variance
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2  # within-participant variance

cat("Variance components:\n")
cat("  Between-participant variance (σ²ᵢ):", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  Within-participant variance (σ²_within):", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Marginal variance (σ²_marginal):", sigma_marginal^2, "\n\n")

# SD of participant average
# Var(avg) = Var((y1+y2+y3+y4)/4)
#          = [σ²ᵢ + σ²_within] / 4  (averaging m observations under random intercept model)
# Under random intercept: Var(y_ij) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within = σ²_marginal
# More precisely: Var(avg_i) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within/m = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)

sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)

cat("SD of participant average:\n")
cat("  SD_avg = σ_marginal * √(ICC + (1-ICC)/m)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = 1 * √(0.4 + 0.6/4)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = √0.55 =", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Effective standardized difference (Cohen's d scale)
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effective standardized difference:\n")
cat("  d = Δ / SD_avg =", delta, "/", sd_avg, "=", effective_d, "\n\n")

# For a two-sample t-test with equal allocation (n per group, total N = 2n):
# Non-centrality parameter: λ = d * √(n/2) where n is per group
# df = 2n - 2

# Function to compute power for given n (per group)
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_level) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  # Non-central t critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_level / 2, df)
  # Power is P(|t| > t_crit | H1)
  power <- pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE) +
           pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n achieving target power
# Start with a reasonable range
n_candidates <- seq(10, 80, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_candidates, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target_power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- n_candidates[min_idx]
achieved_power <- powers[min_idx]

# Also check the preceding design
if (min_idx > 1) {
  preceding_n <- n_candidates[min_idx - 1]
  preceding_power <- powers[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  preceding_n <- NA
  preceding_power <- NA
}

cat("Power calculation results:\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Minimum integer n per group:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", achieved_power, "\n")
if (!is.na(preceding_n)) {

}
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n\n")

# Show a table around the minimum
n_table <- max(min_n - 3, 1):min(min_n + 3, 80)
power_table <- sapply(n_table, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

cat("Power curve around minimum:\n")
for (i in seq_along(n_table)) {
  marker <- if (n_table[i] == min_n) " ← SELECTED" else ""
  cat(sprintf("  n = %3d: power = %.6f%s\n", n_table[i], power_table[i], marker))
}

cat("\n")
cat("Study design summary:\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Sample size: ", min_n, "participants per group\n")
cat("Total participants: ", 2 * min_n, "\n")
cat("Total observations: ", 2 * min_n * m, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant: ", m, "\n")
cat("Marginal SD: ", sigma_marginal, "\n")
cat("ICC: ", rho, "\n")
cat("Group difference: ", delta, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average: ", sd_avg, "\n")
cat("Effective d: ", effective_d, "\n")
cat("Two-sided α: ", alpha, "\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", achieved_power, "\n")

# Study design:
# - Two groups (equal allocation)
# - 4 observations per participant
# - Marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4
# - Group difference = 0.45
# - Analyzed via pooled two-sample t-test on participant averages
# - Target: 90% power, α = 0.05 (two-sided)

library(stats)

# Step 1: Verify variance decomposition
m <- 4
sigma_marginal <- 1
rho <- 0.4  # ICC

# Under random-intercept model:
# Var(y_ij) = sigma_i^2 + sigma_within^2 = sigma_marginal^2
# ICC = sigma_i^2 / sigma_marginal^2

sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2

cat("Variance decomposition verification:\n")
cat("  σ²_i (between) =", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  σ²_within =", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Sum (marginal) =", sigma_i_sq + sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  ICC = σ²_i / σ²_marginal =", sigma_i_sq / sigma_marginal^2, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Variance of participant average
# When averaging m observations from random-intercept model:
# Var(ȳ_i) = Var((1/m) * Σ_j y_ij)
#          = (1/m^2) * Σ_j Cov(y_ij, y_ij) + (1/m^2) * Σ_{j≠k} Cov(y_ij, y_ik)
#          = (1/m^2) * m * (σ²_i + σ²_within) + (1/m^2) * m(m-1) * σ²_i
#          = (1/m) * (σ²_i + σ²_within) + ((m-1)/m) * σ²_i
#          = (1/m) * σ²_marginal + ((m-1)/m) * σ²_i
#          = σ²_marginal * (1/m + ((m-1)/m) * ICC)
#          = σ²_marginal * (1/m + (m-1)*ICC/m)
#          = σ²_marginal * (1 + (m-1)*ICC) / m

var_avg_formula1 <- sigma_marginal^2 * (1 + (m - 1) * rho) / m
sd_avg_formula1 <- sqrt(var_avg_formula1)

# Alternative formulation:
# Var(ȳ_i) = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)
var_avg_formula2 <- sigma_marginal^2 * (rho + (1 - rho) / m)
sd_avg_formula2 <- sqrt(var_avg_formula2)

cat("Variance of participant average (two equivalent formulas):\n")
cat("  Formula 1: σ²_avg = σ²_marginal * (1 + (m-1)*ICC) / m\n")
cat("    Var(ȳ_i) =", var_avg_formula1, "\n")
cat("    SD(ȳ_i) =", sd_avg_formula1, "\n")
cat("  Formula 2: σ²_avg = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)\n")
cat("    Var(ȳ_i) =", var_avg_formula2, "\n")
cat("    SD(ȳ_i) =", sd_avg_formula2, "\n")
cat("  Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(var_avg_formula1, var_avg_formula2)), "\n\n")

sd_avg <- sd_avg_formula1

# Step 3: Effective standardized difference (Cohen's d for t-test)
delta <- 0.45
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effective standardized difference:\n")
cat("  d = Δ / SD(ȳ_i) =", delta, "/", round(sd_avg, 10), "=", effective_d, "\n\n")

# Step 4: Power calculation for two-sample t-test
# For two groups with n per group, total N = 2n
# H0: μ_1 = μ_2, H1: μ_1 ≠ μ_2
# Under H1 with effect d and equal n:
# t ~ t(df = 2n-2, λ) where λ = d * sqrt(n/2)
# Power = P(|t| > t_crit | H1)

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90

compute_power_v2 <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_sig) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  
  # Two-tailed critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_sig / 2, df)
  
  # Power: probability that |t| exceeds critical value under H1
  # This is equivalent to P(t > t_crit | NCP=λ) + P(t < -t_crit | NCP=λ)
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
           pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  return(power)
}

# Test at candidate values around expected minimum
candidates <- 55:65
powers <- sapply(candidates, function(n) compute_power_v2(n, effective_d, alpha))

cat("Power curve (independent calculation):\n")
for (i in seq_along(candidates)) {
  n <- candidates[i]

# Generate data under the random-intercept model and test via two-sample t-test on averages

set.seed(20240515)

m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1
rho <- 0.4
delta <- 0.45
alpha <- 0.05

# Variance components
sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2

cat("Monte Carlo Simulation for Power Validation\n")
cat("===========================================\n")
cat("Data-generating process: random-intercept Gaussian model\n")
cat("  σ²_i (between) =", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  σ²_within =", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Group 1 mean: 0, Group 2 mean:", delta, "\n\n")

# Test for n = 58 and n = 59
test_designs <- c(58, 59)
n_sims <- 10000

results_mc <- data.frame()

for (n_per_group in test_designs) {
  cat("Testing n =", n_per_group, "per group (", n_sims, "simulations)...\n")
  
  rejections <- 0
  
  for (sim in 1:n_sims) {
    # Generate data for group 1
    b_1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, 0, sqrt(sigma_i_sq))  # random intercepts
    y_1 <- matrix(NA, n_per_group, m)
    for (i in 1:n_per_group) {
      y_1[i, ] <- b_1[i] + rnorm(m, 0, sqrt(sigma_within_sq))
    }
    avg_1 <- rowMeans(y_1)
    
    # Generate data for group 2
    b_2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, 0, sqrt(sigma_i_sq))  # random intercepts
    y_2 <- matrix(NA, n_per_group, m)
    for (i in 1:n_per_group) {
      y_2[i, ] <- delta + b_2[i] + rnorm(m, 0, sqrt(sigma_within_sq))
    }
    avg_2 <- rowMeans(y_2)
    
    # Pooled two-sample t-test on participant averages
    t_test <- t.test(avg_1, avg_2, var.equal = TRUE)
    
    if (t_test$p.value < alpha) {
      rejections <- rejections + 1
    }
  }
  
  power_mc <- rejections / n_sims
  se_mc <- sqrt(power_mc * (1 - power_mc) / n_sims)
  ci_lower <- power_mc - 1.96 * se_mc
  ci_upper <- power_mc + 1.96 * se_mc
  
  # Analytical power from previous calculation
  sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)
  effective_d <- delta / sd_avg
  
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- effective_d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)
  power_analytical <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
                      pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  results_mc <- rbind(results_mc, data.frame(
    n_per_group = n_per_group,
    power_mc = power_mc,
    se_mc = se_mc,
    ci_lower = ci_lower,
    ci_upper = ci_upper,
    power_analytical = power_analytical,
    difference = power_mc - power_analytical
  ))

              power_mc, se_mc, ci_lower, ci_upper))
  cat(sprintf("  Analytical: %.6f\n", power_analytical))
  cat(sprintf("  Difference: %.6f\n\n", power_mc - power_analytical))
}

  f <- function(n) {
    df <- 2 * n - 2

    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_sig / 2, df)
    power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
             pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
    return(power - target_p)
  }
  
  # Use uniroot to find n such that power(n) = target_p
  sol <- uniroot(f, interval = c(1, 200), tol = 1e-8)
  return(sol$root)

# Analyze participant averages with two-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05
# Target: 90% power

# Parameters
m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1  # marginal SD
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
delta <- 0.45  # group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level
target_power <- 0.90

# Calculate variance components
# From ICC = sigma_i^2 / sigma_marginal^2
sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2  # between-participant variance
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2  # within-participant variance

cat("Variance components:\n")
cat("  Between-participant variance (σ²ᵢ):", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  Within-participant variance (σ²_within):", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Marginal variance (σ²_marginal):", sigma_marginal^2, "\n\n")

# SD of participant average
# Var(avg) = Var((y1+y2+y3+y4)/4)
#          = [σ²ᵢ + σ²_within] / 4  (averaging m observations under random intercept model)
# Under random intercept: Var(y_ij) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within = σ²_marginal
# More precisely: Var(avg_i) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within/m = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)

sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)

cat("SD of participant average:\n")
cat("  SD_avg = σ_marginal * √(ICC + (1-ICC)/m)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = 1 * √(0.4 + 0.6/4)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = √0.55 =", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Effective standardized difference (Cohen's d scale)
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effective standardized difference:\n")
cat("  d = Δ / SD_avg =", delta, "/", sd_avg, "=", effective_d, "\n\n")

# For a two-sample t-test with equal allocation (n per group, total N = 2n):
# Non-centrality parameter: λ = d * √(n/2) where n is per group
# df = 2n - 2

# Function to compute power for given n (per group)
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_level) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  # Non-central t critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_level / 2, df)
  # Power is P(|t| > t_crit | H1)
  power <- pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE) +
           pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n achieving target power
# Start with a reasonable range

powers <- sapply(n_candidates, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target_power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- n_candidates[min_idx]
achieved_power <- powers[min_idx]

# Also check the preceding design
if (min_idx > 1) {
  preceding_n <- n_candidates[min_idx - 1]
  preceding_power <- powers[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  preceding_n <- NA
  preceding_power <- NA
}

cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Minimum integer n per group:", min_n, "\n")
